title: Declaration, 21 June 1834
cosigners: John Lincoln; Frederick G. Williams; C. K. Morehead; Lyman Wight; Roger Orton; John Sconce; Orson Hyde; James H. Long; John S. Carter; James Collins (+ preface by Cornelius Gilliam)
evidence: Thereafter, Orson Hyde put in writing the same sentiments that JS had expressed verbally, including a proposed settlement to the difficulty, and the statement was signed by JS and five other church members.
notes: Wording drafted by Orson Hyde from JS's oral statement; 11 named authors/signers. ~123 words are Gilliam's prefatory statement and a date by unidentified scribes (not church-authored).

title: History, circa Summer 1832
copy_type: copy in JS Letterbook 1 (JSP: possibly copied from an earlier draft)
evidence: The result was a simple, unpolished account of his first “marvilous experience,” written largely in his own handwriting.
notes: JS hand 983 w (usable as H). Remaining ~1,041 w in F. G. Williams's hand, same first-person JS narrative (S). JSP: hands alternate mid-sentence and JS's quill breaks suggest 'he was copying rather than composing', so even the JS-hand part may be a copy of an earlier JS text.

title: Journal, 1832–1834
copy_type: original journal (holograph + scribes); corpus text is JSP's STANDARDIZED reading text
evidence: Almost half of the entries in the journal were written either entirely or primarily by JS himself; some of the remainder were apparently dictated. … JS and Rigdon recorded in this journal their monthlong trip.
notes: Per-run classification (see report): H 1,692 (JS hand); S 2,092 (other hands, JS first-person singular: Cowdery/Williams incl. JS's Dec 1833 blessings); O 3,195 (Rigdon 814 = Oct 1833 Canada trip in Rigdon's own 'we' voice; Pratt 521; Cowdery 3rd-person/plural entries incl. 11 Jan 1834 prayer 364 = duplicate of prayer doc; Nickerson & misc 169); U 131 (accounts); editorial date headings/page markers 661. Text has modernized spelling/punctuation (JSP clearText for journals), not original orthography.

title: Letter, 30 October 1833
copy_type: printed extract (Evening and the Morning Star, Dec. 1833)
evidence: a church member in Missouri wrote the letter featured here to JS and other church leaders in Kirtland, Ohio. … The authorship of the letter featured here, however, remains uncertain.
notes: NOT BY SMITH: a letter written TO JS by an unidentified Missouri member. Should not be in the Smith class at all.

title: Letter to Church Brethren, 15 June 1835
copy_type: sent original known only from photostat of a photograph
evidence: On 15 June 1835, JS wrote a letter to his “brethren in the Lord.”
notes: Body in W. W. Phelps's hand, signed by JS. JSP attributes to JS but does not describe dictation; Phelps-as-scribe is a stylistic risk.

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Eugene, Indiana, 2 July 1833
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon; Frederick G. Williams (+ postscript by Newel K. Whitney)
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: In the 2 July letter featured here, JS and his counselors in the presidency of the high priesthood sanctioned the prior disciplinary action of the Kirtland bishop’s council.
notes: Presidency letter signed JS, Rigdon, Williams. Whitney postscript = 211 w (O).

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Geneseo, New York, 23 November 1833
evidence: JS on behalf of the Kirtland high priests, Letter
notes: Council letter in first-person plural ('we write in the name of our Lord'); JSP intro also calls it 'JS’s letter of introduction'.

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Jackson County, Missouri, 10 August 1833
evidence: Oliver Cowdery, Letter with postscript by JS … In a postscript, JS added his own words of counsel, expressed sorrow and concern
notes: Body (~931 w) composed by Oliver Cowdery. Only the JS postscript (65 w, 'PS Brethren if I were with you …') is JS (S).

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Jackson County, Missouri, 18 August 1833
evidence: on 18 August, JS personally wrote this lengthy letter of comfort and encouragement to his beleaguered brethren in Missouri.
notes: Entire letter in JS's hand and signed by him.

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Jackson County, Missouri, 2 July 1833
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon (first signer); Frederick G. Williams
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: At one point in the letter, Sidney Rigdon makes a first-person reference to himself, and he was also the first signer of the letter, indicating that he likely served as the principal author.
notes: RIGDON-COMPOSED per JSP. Mostly first-person plural; signed Rigdon, JS, Williams.

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Jackson County, Missouri, 21 April 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: In the letter featured here, written on behalf of the Kirtland leadership, JS accepted the sentiments expressed in that February missive.
notes: Borderline S: signed by JS alone, with first-person-singular postscript; JSP says 'on behalf of' the leadership. Contains an ~85-word revelation (15 Mar 1833, to F. G. Williams) quoted verbatim.

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Jackson County, Missouri, 25 June 1833
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon; Frederick G. Williams; Martin Harris; Orson Hyde (clerk)
evidence: Though in the handwriting of Frederick G. Williams and Orson Hyde, the letter is written primarily in the first-person voice of Sidney Rigdon, who was writing on behalf of the presidency of the high priesthood.
notes: RIGDON-COMPOSED. Text itself: 'I Sidney who write this letter in behalf of the Presidency'. JSP: 'The letter also contains a postscript from JS' = final P.S. (~254 w, first-person plural; mis-tagged 'Signatures' in pages.jsonl).

title: Letter to Church Leaders in Jackson County, Missouri, 6 August 1833
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon (first signer); Frederick G. Williams
evidence: Sidney Rigdon, Frederick G. Williams, and JS, Letter … prompted the presidency of the high priesthood to write this lengthy epistle, which contains the texts of three revelations
notes: ~2,702 of 3,091 w are the texts of three JS revelations (later D&C 97, 94, 98) = revealed register, not prose; only ~390 w of presidency prose (Rigdon first signer).

title: Letter to Church Officers in Clay County, Missouri, 31 August 1835
cosigners: Oliver Cowdery; Sidney Rigdon; Frederick G. Williams; William W. Phelps; John Whitmer
copy_type: later copy (John Whitmer, History, 1837–38); variant copies exist
evidence: On 31 August 1835, “the high council of the presidency of Kirtland and Zion,” including JS, wrote this letter to church officers in Missouri
notes: Six signers incl. Rigdon. JSP: 'Major differences in the three versions are noted herein.' JS postscript to Hezekiah Peck (144 w, 'Dictated by me') is S.

title: Letter to Editor, 22 June 1835
evidence: In this 22 June 1835 letter, JS succinctly stated that the Telegraph had publicized his arraignment and therefore ought to be equally forthcoming about the subsequent trial and acquittal.
notes: Printed text; newspaper typesetting may normalize spelling.

title: Letter to Editor, 5 December 1835
evidence: The same day JS dictated this short letter to the editor, which he intended for public notice
notes: Printed; dictated.

title: Letter to Edward Partridge, 2 May 1833
evidence: This letter from JS in Kirtland, Ohio, to Bishop Edward Partridge in Independence, Missouri, clarified aspects of JS’s nascent economic order
notes: Partridge's contemporaneous copy ('a true copy'); attribution-level S.

title: Letter to Edward Partridge, 5 December 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: JS wrote this 5 December 1833 letter in response to the heartrending and sometimes conflicting reports he received
notes: Ends 'I haste to a close to give room for Bro Oliver' (Cowdery's addition not copied).

title: Letter to Edward Partridge and Others, 10 December 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: JS received these letters on 10 December 1833 and on the same day wrote a letter, featured here, that responded to the more in-depth information his colleagues had sent him.

title: Letter to Edward Partridge and Others, 14 January 1833
cosigners: Orson Hyde; Hyrum Smith (on behalf of a conference of 12 high priests incl. JS)
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: Hyde and Smith composed the letter on 14 January, after which the conference reconvened so that participants could review and approve what they had written.
notes: NOT BY SMITH: composed by Orson Hyde and Hyrum Smith.

title: Letter to Edward Partridge and Others, 30 March 1834
copy_type: contemporaneous copy (Oliver Cowdery letterbook, T. Burdick)
evidence: JS penned a reply to the Missouri leaders on 30 March 1834.
notes: Text: 'I now seat myself to dictate'. Cowdery's postscript = last ~900 w (O); JS portion ~2,375 w.

title: Letter to Emma Smith, 13 October 1832
evidence: This letter is one of the few extant letters written entirely in JS’s own handwriting.

title: Letter to Emma Smith, 18 May 1834
evidence: After the meeting, JS wrote this letter, one of the few surviving letters in his own hand, to Emma.

title: Letter to Emma Smith, 4 June 1834
evidence: JS likely dictated it to Frederick G. Williams, who penned a note at the end of it to his wife, Rebecca Swain Williams.
notes: Dictated; known only from 1839 copy. Last ~305 w are F. G. Williams's note to his own wife (O).

title: Letter to Emma Smith, 6 June 1832
evidence: The letter is one of the few surviving pieces of correspondence written entirely in JS’s own handwriting.

title: Letter to George James, 10 November 1834
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon; Oliver Cowdery (clerk of high council)
evidence: On 10 November 1834, JS and Sidney Rigdon sent a letter to George James
notes: Signed JS and Rigdon; written 'by order of the High Council'.

title: Letter to Hyrum Smith, 3–4 March 1831
evidence: JS included within his letter a copy of a letter from Oliver Cowdery
notes: All in JS's hand, but ~270 of 624 w are JS's copy of Oliver Cowdery's 29 Jan 1831 letter (Cowdery composition, O). JS's own composition ~354 w.

title: Letter to J. G. Fosdick, 3 February 1834
copy_type: contemporaneous copy (Oliver Cowdery letterbook, T. Burdick)
evidence: JS and Orson Hyde, Letter
notes: Signed 'Joseph Smith Jr. (Moderator', 'Orson Hyde (Clerk of Council', 'Copied by direction of the Council' = council letter.

title: Letter to John Hewitt, 14 June 1835
evidence: On 14 June 1835, William W. Phelps wrote this letter to John Hewitt on behalf of the Kirtland, Ohio, high council, which JS presided over.
notes: NOT BY SMITH: Phelps composed and signed it as clerk.

title: Letter to John S. Carter, 13 April 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, JS and F. G. Williams)
evidence: Though signed by both JS and Williams, the letter contains first-person singular pronouns, presumably made by JS as lead author, and statements in first-person plural, as if both JS and Williams were speaking.
notes: JS hand 463 w (usable as H, though copying a joint letter); F. G. Williams hand 563 w (J).

title: Letter to John Smith, 2 July 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, mostly JS hand)
evidence: On 2 July, JS responded with this letter of disapprobation
notes: 237 of 255 w in JS's hand; co-signed by Williams (J character) - JSP also says 'JS and Williams also reiterated'.

title: Letter to John Thornton and Others, 25 June 1834
copy_type: later copy (JS History A-1, W. Richards, 1843; includes redactions)
evidence: On 25 June 1834, while with the Camp of Israel in Clay County, Missouri, JS wrote a letter
notes: Known only from 1843 history copy; JSP does not say wording was altered.

title: Letter to Lyman Wight and Others, 16 August 1834
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: On 16 August 1834, JS wrote this letter to church leaders in Missouri

title: Letter to Martin Harris, 22 February 1831
evidence: In this letter, JS requested that Martin Harris come to Ohio as soon as possible.
notes: RIGDON AS SCRIBE: body in Sidney Rigdon's hand, signed by JS. JSP silent on whether JS dictated or Rigdon drafted. Treat as Rigdon-contaminated.

title: Letter to Moses Daley, circa 8 October 1834
evidence: JS composed a letter to Moses Daley
notes: Excerpt only (92 w).

title: Letter to Moses Nickerson, 19 November 1833
evidence: In this 19 November 1833 letter, JS informed Moses about matters in Kirtland, Ohio
notes: JSP: JS wrote 'apparently because Rigdon had promised to write to Moses but had been unable to do so' - Rigdon not composer/signer/scribe.

title: Letter to Newel Knight and the Church in Colesville, 28 August 1830
evidence: JS and John Whitmer wrote this letter to explain their absence.
notes: Signed John Whitmer and Joseph Smith. Source note: the ca. 1871 manuscript was made 'by copying with some modifications from an earlier draft'.

title: Letter to Noah C. Saxton, 12 February 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: JS wrote this missive to Noah C. Saxton

title: Letter to Noah C. Saxton, 4 January 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: On 4 January 1833, JS wrote a letter to a newspaper editor

title: Letter to Oliver Cowdery, 22 October 1829
copy_type: later copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams, 1832–33)
evidence: JS wrote this letter from Harmony, Pennsylvania, to Oliver Cowdery
notes: Copied ~3 years after sending.

title: Letter to Oliver Cowdery, 24 September 1834
copy_type: printed (Evening and the Morning Star, Sept. 1834)
evidence: The September 1834 issue of The Evening and the Morning Star includes a letter to editor Oliver Cowdery from JS
notes: Printed; Cowdery was the editor.

title: Letter to Oliver Cowdery, December 1834
evidence: this letter from JS to Oliver Cowdery, the newspaper’s editor, discussing the early years of JS’s life
notes: Printed; Cowdery was the editor.

title: Letter to Orson Hyde, 7 April 1834
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: Although the letter is written in JS’s voice, it also contains the signatures of Frederick G. Williams
notes: Co-signature only: JSP also says 'JS composed this letter'. Near-S.

title: Letter to Quorum of the Twelve, 4 August 1835
cosigners: council of presidencies 'and others'; Oliver Cowdery (clerk/scribe)
evidence: a council consisting of members of the presidency of the high priesthood, the presidency of the Missouri high council, “and others” composed a letter to the Twelve Apostles
notes: Cowdery 'presumably served as scribe'; JS signed as moderator and added a postscript to William Smith (120 w). Rigdon not named but was in the presidency.

title: Letter to Sally Waterman Phelps, 20 July 1835
evidence: handwriting and signature of JS
notes: Note added by JS to a W. W. Phelps letter; transcribed from a photograph.

title: Letter to Silas Smith, 26 September 1833
evidence: JS wrote this 26 September 1833 letter, defending the idea of modern-day revelation, to his uncle Silas Smith
notes: 1855 copy; JSP judges it 'the most complete and accurate extant copy' (Coray copy differs). HAND CONFLICT: JSP says handwriting of Jesse Smith, but pages 2-4 are tagged Frederick G. Williams (from JSP page metadata) in pages.jsonl/meta.json.

title: Letter to the Church, circa April 1834
copy_type: printed (Evening and the Morning Star, Apr. 1834)
evidence: The author attribution “Elders of the Church in Kirtland” likely refers to JS and other church leaders.
notes: Collective authorship; Rigdon not named but cannot be excluded.

title: Letter to the Church, circa February 1834
copy_type: printed (Evening and the Morning Star, Feb. 1834)
evidence: The articles, written as epistles from JS and other leaders in Kirtland, Ohio, focus on major doctrinal themes
notes: Collective authorship; Rigdon not named but cannot be excluded. HAND CONFLICT: printed text, but page 2 (2,046 w) tagged 'Frederick G. Williams' in meta.json (Williams was the Star's printer).

title: Letter to the Church, circa March 1834
copy_type: printed (Evening and the Morning Star, Mar. 1834)
evidence: JS and the other elders responsible for writing this letter also expounded upon several other themes
notes: Collective authorship; Rigdon not named but cannot be excluded. JSP: ideas of the Silas Smith letter 'appeared again in the second installment' (this one).

title: Letter to the Church in Clay County, Missouri, 22 January 1834
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon; Frederick G. Williams (signed by Orson Hyde as clerk)
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: JS, Sidney Rigdon, and Frederick G. Williams wrote this 22 January 1834 letter
notes: Presidency letter incl. Rigdon.

title: Letter to the Church in Colesville, 2 December 1830
evidence: At the time JS and John Whitmer wrote it
notes: Last ~318 w are a copy of Oliver Cowdery's 12 Nov 1830 letter plus John Whitmer's note (O). 1871 copy 'with some modifications'.

title: Letter to the Church in Thompson, Ohio, 6 February 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: In the letter featured here, JS and his counselors in the presidency of the high priesthood announced that Salmon Gee had been appointed to preside over the church in Thompson.
notes: Signed JS, Rigdon, Williams.

title: Letter to the Church, not after 18 December 1833
copy_type: printed (Evening and the Morning Star, Dec. 1833)
evidence: The letter was sent “from the elders in Kirtland,” including JS.
notes: Collective; Rigdon not named but cannot be excluded.

title: Letter to the Elders of the Church, 16 November 1835
evidence: JS dictated this letter, probably to his scribe, Warren Parrish.

title: Letter to the Elders of the Church, 2 October 1835
evidence: JS wrote this first installment on 2 October and submitted it to editor John Whitmer

title: Letter to the Elders of the Church, 30 November–1 December 1835
evidence: it is not clear whether JS or his scribe Warren Parrish penned this letter. … he would have dictated to or otherwise worked with Parrish to compose the letter
notes: Borderline S/J: JSP allows that Parrish helped compose.

title: Letter to Vienna Jaques, 4 September 1833
evidence: JS stated that both Jaques’s earlier letter and his own spiritual promptings led him to write the letter featured here.
notes: Later docket wrongly claims the letter was 'written by Joseph Smith’s own hand'; JSP: handwriting of F. G. Williams.

title: Letter to William Smith, circa 18 December 1835
evidence: He was at home and wrote the above letter, or rather indited it, to his brother William.
notes: Dictated ('indited').

title: Letter to William W. Phelps, 11 January 1833
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, F. G. Williams)
evidence: On 11 January 1833, JS wrote a letter to William W. Phelps in Missouri

title: Letter to William W. Phelps, 27 November 1832
copy_type: retained copy (JS Letterbook 1, JS and F. G. Williams)
evidence: The present letter, which was written by JS to William W. Phelps on 27 November 1832
notes: JS hand 637 w (usable as H); F. G. Williams 462 w. History-1832 intro adds the letter was one 'which JS originally dictated'. Contains a revelatory passage ('thus saith the still small voice', later D&C 85).

title: Letter to William W. Phelps, 31 July 1832
copy_type: retained copy (F. G. Williams, signed by JS)
evidence: On the morning of 31 July, JS dictated this letter to Frederick G. Williams, his recently appointed scribe

title: Letters to John Burk, Sally Waterman Phelps, and Almira Mack Scobey, 1–2 June 1835
cosigners: Oliver Cowdery; William W. Phelps; John Whitmer
evidence: Phelps then served as the scribe for this letter—signed by himself, JS, Cowdery, and Whitmer—informing Burk of that decision.
notes: Three items: council letter to Burk (~970 w, J, Phelps scribe); Phelps's own letter to his wife (~1,132 w, O, not Smith); JS note to Almira Scobey (138 w JS hand, H).

title: Prayer, 11 January 1834
cosigners: Frederick G. Williams; Newel K. Whitney; John Johnson; Oliver Cowdery; Orson Hyde
evidence: This prayer by JS and five of his close associates addressed several related concerns
notes: Narrated in third person ('our brother Joseph'). DUPLICATE: the same prayer (~364 w) is also inside journal-1832-1834.

title: Preface to Book of Mormon, circa August 1829, Page iii
evidence: In the preface, JS addressed false rumors about the Book of Mormon, briefly described how the pages were lost, and quoted the revelation concerning the missing manuscript.
notes: Signed 'The Author'; includes quoted revelation text.

title: Testimony, circa 2 November 1831
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon (first signer); Orson Hyde; William E. McLellin; Luke Johnson; Lyman Johnson; + 12 later signers
evidence: The circumstances surrounding the production of this testimony are ambiguous. … JS then dictated a “testimony” of the divine origin of his revelations for the elders to sign.
notes: Source note credits no author ('Testimony … signed by Sidney Rigdon …'); the JS-dictation claim comes from the later 1838 history. Copied as '73 Revelation' (revelatory register).

title: Smith History 1838 (JS-H), LDS 2013 edition
cosigners: Sidney Rigdon; George W. Robinson (1838 draft); James Mulholland, Robert B. Thompson (1839–41 drafts/copies)
copy_type: later edited copy (Draft 2 1839 -> Manuscript History A-1 -> Times and Seasons 1842 -> Pearl of Great Price 1851/1880/1981/2013)
evidence: Serving as principal sources for this version of the history were the manuscript that JS, Sidney Rigdon, and George W. Robinson had created in Missouri in 1838, and Draft 1.
notes: Evidence NOT in local data: quoted from JSP web page 'History, circa June 1839–circa 1841 [Draft 2]' (historical intro), fetched 2026-11-17. Same page: preamble 'added in 1839 when' Mulholland 'wrote Draft 2'; manuscript 'emended at several times by various scribes'. Corpus text is the modern 2013 edition: contains editorial '[1838]', ellipsis '…' marking omitted text, KJV quotations of Moroni and a quoted Martin Harris account.
